subject: Post-demo: parallel connections, quota and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@brightwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: parallel connections, quota and next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the right Redwood offering for BrightWave:

1) Goals / SLO targets you mentioned
   - Sustained concurrent streaming sessions: ~200
   - Peak parallel requests (short bursts): up to ~600 for 2-3 minutes
   - Token throughput: target ~15k tokens/min during peak
   - Latency requirement: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens)

2) Implementation notes we heard from your infra team
   - Client uses WebSocket + SSE for streaming outputs
   - Long-lived connections with fairly aggressive keep-alives
   - Frontend connection pooling per browser instance (est. 8 sockets/user)

3) Open questions we need answers on to propose a concrete quota/price:
   - Are the 200 concurrent sessions per-region or global?
   - Expected sustained QPS (RPS) outside burst windows?
   - Any hard cap on open TCP/socket counts from your LB or proxies?

Next steps from our side: I attached a brief proposal that outlines two options — Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) and a simpler hosted quota plan with elevated rate limits. Please see attached Redwood-parallel-connections-proposal.pdf.

Could you confirm the three answers above and share any infra constraints by EOD Monday PST? Once we have that, Karthik and Marissa will put together a recommended quota + trial plan.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-parallel-connections-proposal.pdf]
From: Samantha Park <samantha@brightwave.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan@brightwave.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 18:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: parallel connections, quota and next steps

Diego —

Great recap, appreciated. Answers below based on our infra check with the platform team:

- Concurrency: the 200 concurrent streaming sessions are regional (US-east primarily) but we may replicate to EU later. The production cutover will be US-first.
- Sustained QPS: outside bursts we expect ~50-80 requests/sec (~3k-5k tokens/sec). Bursts to 600 requests are expected during synchronous user events (campaign launches).
- Socket caps: our LB (NGINX + internal proxy) currently allows ~1,000 open connections per service instance. We plan to run multiple instances (2-3) behind the LB.

Streaming: we use per-request chunked output so low-latency streaming is important; clients expect token-level updates within ~50-100ms.

Procurement timeline: we’d like pricing and a trial plan by next Wednesday (Mar 10). Attaching an infra diagram to help you size.

Thanks,
Samantha Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightWave Analytics

Goal: have a short proposal + numbers by Monday EOD so I can send to BrightWave (they want pricing by Mar 10).

Diego

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Diego / Marissa —

Quick analysis after reviewing their infra diagram and the numbers Samantha provided:

Summary recommendation:
- Offer Dedicated trial: Reserved pool of 250 concurrent streaming sessions (US-east) to give headroom above 200 target.
- Configure connection pooling guidance: recommend per-instance max sockets ~400 and 2-3 instances behind LB (matches their plan).
- Host-rate model: hybrid token + request limits. Enforce a request-rate soft quota of 1,200 req/min with burst to 2,000 req/min for up to 120 seconds (leaky-bucket). Token-rate quota 100k tokens/min for the tenant during trial.
- Streaming SLO: we can meet token-chunk dispatch within 50-120ms p95 on Dedicated in us-east (depends on model selection).

Operational notes / risk:
- Long-lived WS connections increase socket churn and memory usage on inference nodes. Must ensure keep-alive timeouts align (recommend 60s).
- If they multiplex many user sessions per browser instance, we should instrument prefix caching and recommend KV cache warmups for common prompts to reduce token compute.

Attachments: I did a quick sizing calc and put numbers in connpool-sizing-calculation.xlsx (est. 3 x A10x like instances with 250 reserved streams).

Suggested commercial approach to propose Monday:
- 30-day Dedicated trial: $Xk/month (TBD by pricing) with included monitoring and 5 dedicated GPU nodes; overage at token-rate pricing.
- Fallback hosted plan: Elevated hosted quota with soft limits (1,200 req/min) and a shallow SLA.

I can prepare an engineering appendix that describes the leaky-bucket settings and socket recommendations.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: connpool-sizing-calculation.xlsx]
